purpose: Own concise extract of audited sources and the accepted application policy. Full publications and the private prototype are not distributed.
ownerDecision: The owner accepted mock04 and implementation on 2026-10-25: a separate orienting upper-only LH comparison, qualified clinical information, a current result point without a median in childhood gaps, and a closed-panel censored source note.
clinicalImpact: New prospective comparison and information. Actual method-specific reference intervals and biochemical classification data remain unchanged. New records preserve their own versioned comparison; older records are not recalculated.

applicationPolicy.stage: Current typed G1/Th1 or absent observation. No stage inference from age, P/Ax or LH; known G/Th2–5 excluded.
applicationPolicy.sourceRole: Accepted application orienting reference supported by the Labcorp age-row upper value, not a validated universal RI or Tanner-stage profile.
applicationPolicy.context: Current patient; basal serum scope. Known hormonal treatment/stimulation/incompatible context retain meaning. Unknown method, time, specimen and therapy do not become confirmed facts.
notImported: female TannerI upper0.18 as a shared profile
applicationPolicy.stageGuard: Explicit rejected, stale, wrong-feature or P observation cannot masquerade as missing stage. Known valid assay permits only orienting comparison, malformed assay fails closed.

sources.citation: Bangalore Krishna K, Garibaldi L. Front Pediatr12:1504874, published2025-01-21
sources.finding: Review >=0.3IU/L for hormonal puberty onset in appropriate HS-IFMA/HS-ICMA is a diagnostic threshold, not a universal reference percentile. Low LH does not exclude early activation.
sources.limitations: Method, sampling and clinical selection matter; limited boys evidence. Cannot directly generalise girl CPP cohorts to all boys1–6/G1 or unknown methods. Diagnostic0.5 for less-sensitive assays does not justify Mayo's RI0.5.

sources.citation: Howard SR. Interpretation of reproductive hormones before, during and after the pubertal transition—Identifying health and disordered puberty. Clin Endocrinol95:702–716,2021
sources.finding: Method-dependent thresholds; biochemical activation may precede visibleG2/Th2. Low basal LH does not exclude CPP.
sources.limitations: Review description <0.1IU/L is not a verified empirical P97.5 for all healthy children1–6 or all assays.

sources.citation: Central precocious puberty: an Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline. JCEM111(8):2101–2144,2026
sources.location: Entire Question3, Recommendation3, benefits/harms, additional/research considerations; related reviewdgag169 Question3 and correctiondgag320 also read.
sources.finding: Conditional very-low-certainty recommendation for ultrasensitive basal LH in suspected CPP; method/stage-specific diagnostic examples, not a universal RI. Low LH does not exclude CPP.
sources.limitations: Predominantly girlB2/B3 evidence, scarce boys data. No universal proof for boys1–6 or G1/Th1. Method detection <0.05–0.1IU/L is not an upper RI.

sources.citation: Wiedemann G, Jonetz-Mentzel L, Panse R. Establishment of Reference Ranges for Follitropin and Lutropin in Neonates, Infants, Children and Adolescents.1993;31(6):395–401
sources.population: Both sexes pooled2–11years, N282; not N under6 or each sex. No verified typed TannerI restriction.
sources.materialMethod: Serum08–10, Abbott IMx MEIA, WHO68/40. Source sensitivity0.07U/L, not retrospectively labelled formalLOQ.
sources.censoring: Authors replaced below-sensitivity observations with the method boundary, retaining<. Exact latent median unknown.
sources.limitations: No1–<2 coverage; whole broad age group, not continuous age P50 or individual trajectory. Historical method not automatically comparable. Source RI and numeric median not imported.
